fabrication_guard: Structural descriptions only — no clause text reproduced verbatim. All descriptions are paraphrased summaries of requirements.

4.1.title: Understanding the organisation and its context
4.1.description: The organisation shall determine internal and external issues relevant to its purpose and strategic direction that affect its ability to achieve intended QMS outcomes.
common_ncs: Context not reviewed at planned intervals
Issues not linked to QMS scope

4.2.title: Understanding the needs and expectations of interested parties
4.2.description: The organisation shall determine interested parties relevant to the QMS and their relevant requirements, and monitor and review this information.

4.3.title: Determining the scope of the QMS
4.3.description: The organisation shall determine the boundaries and applicability of the QMS. The scope shall state products/services covered and justify any exclusions (Cl.8 only).
common_ncs: Scope does not reflect actual operations

4.4.title: Quality management system and its processes
4.4.description: The organisation shall establish, implement, maintain and continually improve the QMS, including determining processes needed and their sequence, interaction, inputs, outputs, resources, responsibilities, risks and opportunities, and performance indicators.

5.1.title: Leadership and commitment
5.1.description: Top management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment to the QMS by taking accountability, ensuring policy and objectives are established, ensuring integration with business processes, promoting process approach and risk-based thinking, and ensuring resources are available.
mandatory_evidence: QMS policy signed by top management
common_ncs: Policy not reviewed by top management

5.2.title: Quality policy
5.2.description: Top management shall establish a quality policy appropriate to the organisation's purpose, including commitment to applicable requirements and continual improvement. The policy shall be available as documented information, communicated, understood and available to interested parties.
mandatory_evidence: Evidence staff are aware of policy
common_ncs: Policy does not reference continual improvement

5.3.title: Organisational roles, responsibilities and authorities
5.3.description: Top management shall assign, communicate and ensure responsibility and authority for ensuring QMS conformity, reporting QMS performance, promoting customer focus, and maintaining QMS integrity during change.

6.1.title: Actions to address risks and opportunities
6.1.description: The organisation shall determine risks and opportunities from context and interested parties analysis, and plan actions to address them, integrated into QMS processes, with evaluation of effectiveness.
mandatory_evidence: Evidence actions taken and effectiveness evaluated
common_ncs: Risks not linked to context analysis

6.2.title: Quality objectives and planning to achieve them
6.2.description: Quality objectives shall be established at relevant functions, levels and processes. They shall be measurable, consistent with quality policy, monitored, communicated and updated. Planning shall determine what, resources, who, when and how results will be evaluated.

6.3.title: Planning of changes
6.3.description: Changes to the QMS shall be carried out in a planned manner considering purpose, consequences for integrity, resource availability, and allocation of responsibilities.

7.1.title: Resources
7.1.description: The organisation shall determine and provide resources needed for the QMS including people, infrastructure, process environment, monitoring and measurement resources, and organisational knowledge.

7.2.title: Competence
7.2.description: The organisation shall determine necessary competence for persons affecting quality performance, ensure they are competent based on education, training or experience, take actions where applicable, and retain documented information as evidence.

7.3.title: Awareness
7.3.description: Persons working under the organisation's control shall be aware of quality policy, relevant objectives, their contribution to QMS effectiveness, and implications of not conforming.

7.4.title: Communication
7.4.description: The organisation shall determine internal and external communications relevant to the QMS including what, when, with whom, how, and who communicates.

7.5.title: Documented information
7.5.description: The QMS shall include documented information required by the standard and determined necessary by the organisation. Documented information shall be controlled for availability, suitability, protection, distribution, storage, retrieval, and disposition.
mandatory_evidence: Records of document review and approval

8.1.title: Operational planning and control
8.1.description: The organisation shall plan, implement, control, maintain and retain documented information for processes needed to meet requirements, including establishing criteria for processes and products, controlling processes to the criteria, and controlling planned changes.

8.2.title: Requirements for products and services
8.2.description: The organisation shall ensure requirements for products and services are determined, including legal/regulatory requirements. Customer communication, review of requirements before commitment, and changes to requirements shall be controlled.

8.3.title: Design and development of products and services
8.3.description: The organisation shall establish a design and development process including planning, inputs, controls (reviews, verification, validation), outputs, and change control. Design changes shall be identified, reviewed and controlled.

8.4.title: Control of externally provided processes, products and services
8.4.description: The organisation shall ensure externally provided processes, products and services conform to requirements. Controls shall include supplier evaluation, monitoring of performance, and communication of requirements to external providers.

8.5.title: Production and service provision
8.5.description: Production and service provision shall be implemented under controlled conditions including documented information, suitable monitoring resources, infrastructure, competent persons, validation where output cannot be verified, measures to prevent human error, and release/delivery/post-delivery activities.

8.6.title: Release of products and services
8.6.description: The organisation shall implement planned arrangements at appropriate stages to verify product/service requirements have been met. Evidence of conformity and traceability to authorising person shall be retained.

8.7.title: Control of nonconforming outputs
8.7.description: Outputs not conforming to requirements shall be identified and controlled to prevent unintended use or delivery. Actions shall include correction, segregation, return or suspension. Nonconforming outputs released under concession shall be authorised.

9.1.title: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
9.1.description: The organisation shall determine what needs to be monitored and measured, methods for valid results, when monitoring/measurement shall be performed and analysed, and when results shall be reported. Customer satisfaction shall be monitored.

9.2.title: Internal audit
9.2.description: The organisation shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on QMS conformity and effective implementation. An audit programme shall consider importance of processes, changes affecting the organisation, and results of previous audits.
common_ncs: Audits not conducted at planned intervals

9.3.title: Management review
9.3.description: Top management shall review the QMS at planned intervals to ensure suitability, adequacy, effectiveness and alignment with strategic direction. Inputs and outputs shall meet specified requirements.
mandatory_evidence: Evidence of all mandatory inputs reviewed

10.1.title: Improvement — General
10.1.description: The organisation shall determine and select opportunities for improvement and implement actions to meet customer requirements and enhance satisfaction.

10.2.title: Nonconformity and corrective action
10.2.description: The organisation shall react to nonconformities by taking action, evaluating need for corrective action, implementing action, reviewing effectiveness, updating risks and opportunities, and making changes to QMS if necessary. Root cause shall be determined. Documented information shall be retained.

10.3.title: Continual improvement
10.3.description: The organisation shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the QMS using results of analysis, evaluation, management review outputs and audit results.
mandatory_evidence: Trend data showing improvement over time
common_ncs: Management review outputs not acted upon
